subject.title: Plugin `message_sending` hooks silently bypassed on channel agent-reply delivery paths (2026.5.26, still present in 2026.6.1)

question: Which canonical branch should own the `message_sending` safety-hook repair for configured dispatcher paths and Telegram streamed-final delivery?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible, but the safe fix changes a documented pre-send safety boundary and multiple open PRs make different exactly-once tradeoffs; automation should not choose that ownership model alone.

options.title: Adopt repaired broad branch
options.body: Select `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93216` as canonical after its suffix/draft/conflict/proof gaps are repaired, because it covers both the dispatcher seam and Telegram streamed-final path.

options.title: Land a narrow dispatcher fix first
options.body: Use a smaller dispatcher-only PR such as `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92976` or `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92762`, while explicitly leaving streamed-final coverage tracked on this issue.

options.title: Replace with a fresh owner patch
options.body: Close or pause overlapping branches and ask for a new focused patch that preserves Telegram delivery context and documents the exactly-once ownership boundary.

recommendation.title: Adopt repaired broad branch
recommendation.body: Select `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93216` as canonical after its suffix/draft/conflict/proof gaps are repaired, because it covers both the dispatcher seam and Telegram streamed-final path.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the broad open candidate branch that most directly matches the issue's full dispatcher plus Telegram streamed-final scope.
